description.narrative: Expand the sustainable tourism business chain around and within protected areas of high value for biodiversity conservation in the Atlantic Forest Great Reserve
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The Atlantic Forest Great Reserve project aims to foster sustainable economic development in communities located in key areas for biodiversity conservation. By advancing sustainable tourism and responsible production chains within and around Protected Areas (PAs), the initiative seeks to create stable income opportunities, enhance social inclusion, and strengthen local enterprises. Communities in the surrounding regions will benefit directly through job creation and training, skills development, and expanded economic opportunities tied to environmental stewardship. The project also emphasizes the valorization of traditional knowledge and the strengthening of local governance systems, with a focus on gender equity and the inclusion of youth. By positioning biodiversity as a core economic asset, the project supports the diversification of local economies, the growth of sustainable businesses, and the reduction of reliance on environmentally harmful practices. Its close collaboration with Protected Areas helps to safeguard endangered species and highlights natural capital as a driver of regional development. In addition, the initiative promotes ecotourism as a catalyst for income generation, building partnerships among local communities, the private sector, and public authorities. This integrated strategy combines environmental conservation with improved quality of life, fostering social inclusion, economic resilience, and sustainable development in one of Brazil’s most valuable biomes.
